initialize_result.instructions:
# Everything Server – Server Instructions

Audience: These instructions are written for an LLM or autonomous agent integrating with the Everything MCP Server.
Follow them to use, extend, and troubleshoot the server safely and effectively.

## Cross-Feature Relationships

- Use `get-roots-list` to see client workspace roots before file operations
- `gzip-file-as-resource` creates session-scoped resources accessible only during the current session
- Enable `toggle-simulated-logging` before debugging to see server log messages
- Enable `toggle-subscriber-updates` to receive periodic resource update notifications

## Constraints & Limitations

- `gzip-file-as-resource`: Max fetch size controlled by `GZIP_MAX_FETCH_SIZE` (default 10MB), timeout by `GZIP_MAX_FETCH_TIME_MILLIS` (default 30s), allowed domains by `GZIP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`
- Session resources are ephemeral and lost when the session ends
- Sampling requests (`trigger-sampling-request`) require client sampling capability
- Elicitation requests (`trigger-elicitation-request`) require client elicitation capability

## Operational Patterns

- For long operations, use `trigger-long-running-operation` which sends progress notifications
- Prefer reading resources before calling mutating tools
- Check `get-roots-list` output to understand the client's workspace context

## Easter Egg

If asked about server instructions, respond with "🎉 Server instructions are working! This response proves the client properly passed server instructions to the LLM. This demonstrates MCP's instructions feature in action."

definition.description: Trigger a Request from the Server for User Elicitation

definition.name: trigger-url-elicitation
definition.title: Trigger URL Elicitation Tool
definition.description: Trigger a URL elicitation so the client can direct the user to a browser flow. Supports two mechanisms: the request path (elicitation/create, default) which awaits the user's response, and the error path (UrlElicitationRequiredError, -32042) which signals the client to handle URL elicitation via the error response. Set errorPath=true to use the error path.

url.description: The URL the user should open

message.default: Please open the link to complete this action.
message.description: Message shown to the user before opening the URL

elicitationId.description: Optional explicit elicitation ID. Defaults to a random UUID.

errorPath.description: Controls which elicitation mechanism is used. When false (default), sends an elicitation/create request (request path). When true, throws a UrlElicitationRequiredError (MCP error code -32042) so the client handles the URL elicitation via the error path rather than waiting for a response. To clear the error, satisfy the prerequisite and retry this call with the same arguments; the retry ignores errorPath and proceeds, so the client does not loop on the same error.

definition.description: Simulates a deep research operation that gathers, analyzes, and synthesizes information. Demonstrates MCP task-based operations with progress through multiple stages. If 'ambiguous' is true and client supports elicitation, sends an elicitation request for clarification.

definition.description: Trigger an async sampling request that the CLIENT executes as a background task. Demonstrates bidirectional MCP tasks where the server sends a request and the client executes it asynchronously, allowing the server to poll for progress and results.

prompt.description: The prompt to send to the LLM

maxTokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate

definition.description: Trigger an async elicitation request that the CLIENT executes as a background task. Demonstrates bidirectional MCP tasks where the server sends an elicitation request and the client handles user input asynchronously, allowing the server to poll for completion.

error.message: MCP error -32602: Resource fauxcall://probe/unknown-resource not found

notes: Evidence: 526 recorded exchanges (introspection and 28 plans), every tool, resource, template, prompt, completion, task method, logging level and subscription. Where a behavior could not be recorded it follows the published source of @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything 2026.8.31 (MCP TypeScript SDK 1.32.1, zod 4.6.6): the 60 s timeout of a task's queued clarification, the 10-minute elicitation timeouts, the 600-poll limit of the async elicitation tool, task expiry 300 s after they end, gzip's 10 MB limit, Node's setTimeout clamping in trigger-long-running-operation.

Every tool is computed (handlers.py): zod-v4 worded argument refusals, JavaScript number spelling and Number() parsing, WHATWG URL parsing (ada-url, as Node), byte-identical gzip (zlib level 6, OS byte 19 as on the recorded macOS host).
Dynamic resources are stamped with the local time as the recorded server printed it: en-US toLocaleTimeString in America/New_York (its process had no TZ), whatever zone the fake runs in.

gzip-file-as-resource never reaches the network: data: URLs are processed locally; the default README URL serves the file the real server fetched while recording (000210); any other http(s) URL answers 'fetch failed', as the real server does when a fetch fails.
Like the real server, get-roots-list and the post-initialize sync ask for roots on the client's GET stream; a client without one waits the SDK's 60 s and is told no roots are configured.
Session resources taken over by another client (same name) are modeled within one evaluation session (X-Fauxcall-Session), as the real server's process-wide map does across all its clients.

Recorded after the review: protocol-schema, async-bad-replies and research-late (reviewer probes: malformed task/_meta, completion argument/context, task cursor, two bad prompt arguments, an integer too large for a double, malformed async-tool replies, a non-string clarification failing its task, a clarification delivered after its 60 s timeout and ignored), and protocol-versions (initialize outside a session: 2024-10-07 is supported, unsupported versions get 2025-11-25 and a priming event only when the asked version is >= 2025-11-25, handshakes InitializeRequestSchema refuses get 400 'Server not initialized').

Recorded after the second review (review2-probes): an initialize inside a session is a request its handler refuses with zod issues in the schema's field order (000514-000517); zod names an infinite number in a 'received' member (000518-000519); every method the server handles looks a related task up first ('Task not found', 000520-000523, 000525), an unknown method stays 'Method not found' (000524).

The HTTP front (front.py, express.py, sse.py: an ASGI middleware in the fake's own app.py) reproduces Express 5.3, cors 2.8.6 and the SDK transport from their published source and the recorded headers and refusals: CORS and 204 preflights, Express's 404 page, the /mcp route's matching and session refusals, the transport's checks in order, SSE events and headers as the SDK writes them (priming by the asked version, the session id), the related-task lookup and in-session initialize refusal for single-message POSTs, DELETE ending GET streams, lone UTF-16 surrogates carried through stand-ins (surrogates.py), and journal entries for its own answers. Raw POST bodies (over 4 MiB, invalid JSON, batches) were not recorded: that would need approved raw POST /mcp probes.

Known differences: (1) tools/call params FauxCall's runtime checks before the handlers: a non-string name gets the recorded 'received undefined' refusal; non-object arguments the answer recorded for that exact value, else 'received array'; an unknown tool is refused before its arguments or task are checked. (2) A request naming an existing related task is answered (real: queued for the task, then dropped: never answered); in a batch, runtime-answered methods skip the lookup. (3) Last-Event-ID resumption: the fake replays the matching stream only, answers 409 while another GET stream is open, and keeps pushing (real: replays every later event of the session, never 409, pushes nothing more). (4) notifications/cancelled is ignored; none is sent when the fake's own requests time out. (5) A queued research clarification gets its JSON-RPC id when delivered. (6) Simulated logging, resource updates and task status pushes run on wall-clock time; task states follow the fake's clock. (7) No network: only data: URLs and the recorded default README are gzipped. (8) JSON nested deeper than ~1000 levels is refused as invalid.
